children: swung 3.7% as investors reacted to the casino company's third-quarter earnings report. Consolidated net revenue was up 2.8% year over year to $488.7M, which beat analyst forecasts, and was driven by record Las Vegas market revenue of $479.1M. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA declined 4.3% during the quarter to $182.6M, impacted by higher utility costs and $5.8M in one-time expenses tied to the company's 50th-anniversary celebrations.

The company said operating momentum has been boosted by the successful October 27 opening of the North Fork property, which began contributing management fees. Meanwhile, management raised full-year 2026 capital expenditures to between $550M and $570M, citing Green Valley Ranch cost overruns and an expanded scope for the Durango North expansion project.

CBRE Equity Research analyst John DeCree highlighted that the quarter was relatively in line with expectations, but investors fixated on the ~200 bps of margin decline in Las Vegas that occurred despite the topline growth. DeCree and his team believe the opening of North Fork provides an upside surprise to investors. He highlighted that Red Rock Resorts

has a long and successful track record of developing, opening, and managing Native American casinos. The firm anticipates a rapid ramp of cash flow from fee income emanating from the property. "Further, RRR still has an $86M receivable for development advances to the tribe that now move from PIK to cash-paying interest and principal, providing additional near-term cash flow and an inevitable capital return, likely when the project is recapitalized," updated DeCree.
For investors, DeCree thinks shares of Red Rock Resorts

remain compelling at current levels, trading at 26% off the 52-week highs. The CBRE view is that the market is underestimating the cash flow potential at North Fork, which is finally open and should begin to ramp meaningfully throughout FY27.

title: Red Rock Resorts is defended by CBRE after a post-earnings stumble
